newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's wheat, maize futures drop on surpluses.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's wheat, maize futures drop on surpluses.

text.p: Wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange reversed a rising trend on Tuesday on news suggesting neither the domestic nor the international markets were buyers for vast surplus stocks, traders said.

"Hardly anything went out of the country and people are getting increasingly aware of that," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex. "They realise the country is full of flour and wheat, and the mills are competing in driving wheat prices down."
Traders said Hungary had a wheat surplus of several thousand tonnes and recent news about potential exports to Bulgaria and Romania proved unfounded.

They said the market was flooded by offers for the sale of 500 lots of 1996 wheat crop without any buyers and the settlement price of May milling wheat closed 550 forints down at 25,100 forints in meagre turnover.
Futures prices for the 1997 wheat crop were mostly unaffected by the selling wave as two brokerages bought in large amounts, traders said.
The most actively traded August maturity closed only 40 forints down, at 22,000 forints.
Maize futures continued to ease, also depressed by large surplus stocks in Hungary.
"We had too large a crop last year, and there were no substantial exports," Szoke said.
